steps.text: Blend the lime juice, vinegar, and cilantro together in a blender until smooth. Add the brown sugar, garlic, and salt; blend again until smooth. Spoon the mustard into the mixture. Turn the blender on and slowly pour the olive oil into the dressing mixture in a thin stream; blend until thoroughly combined.

raw_recipe.headline: Lime-Cilantro Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: This deliciously tangy vinaigrette is versatile enough to be used for both mixed green or taco salads.
raw_recipe.name: Lime-Cilantro Vinaigrette

review.reviewBody: I've been making salads all summer and I like to make my salad dressings homemade. This recipe caught my eye as I love cilantro and always have some in the fridge waiting to be used. The only change I made was I used Dijon mustard instead of spicy brown mustard. Next time will add some color to my salad, like cherry tomatoes. My salad ingredients were mixed greens, avocado, red onion and sliced chicken breast and feta. This salad dressing is a bright green and has a crisp fresh flavor.

Great to use for summer entertaining. 

The only change I made to the lime-cilantro dressing was to add a dash of chipotle chili powder and a dash of cumin. Before adding these, the recipe was a little too "bright" and needed some smokiness.

I used this recipe over a layered taco salad that included tri-colored tortilla strips, black beans, corn, Chopped tomatoes, quartered & seeded cucumber slices, Mexican cheese, lime wedges (garnish), avocado slices. I made the Key West chicken recipe from Allrecipes, as another person suggested. I LOVE these two recipes together!

I think this Key West chicken and a little of the lime-cilantro dressing drizzled over it could be pretty versatile together, even in different dishes.

(I cooked the chicken on a grill pan and then cut it into strips to serve with the salad. With the taco salad, I also served taco-seasoned ground beef and had a bottle of Catalina dressing on hand, so people could go “old school” with their taco salad, if they wanted to do so, instead of using the chicken and lime-cilantro vinagrette. (The Catalina bottle never got opened, though :)

I also made taco bowls by putting 10-inch flour tortillas over soup cans in the oven, on a baking sheet, baking @ 400 for 10 min, then letting cool completely so they retain their shape.

Its wonderful! But I tweaked it a bit. Instead of olive oil I substituted 1/2 cup coconut yogurt. I also added two tablespoons of spicy brown mustard instead of just 3/4 tsp. I also think it would be great with any mustard you choose, any yogurt you choose instead of oil, and as much garlic as you like! What's key for sure is the fresh squeezed lime juice and the fresh cilantro! Awesome recipe! Thanks! :-)

This was really a great dressing. I did alter the ingredients slightly though, instead of white vinegar I used organic apple cider vinegar and I used 1T maple syrup instead of the brown sugar. Tasty! Will be using again!

Very simple preparation; I used my stick blender to cut down on cleanup. I also cut the oil by 1/4 to make the final product a little lower in calories. The taste is pretty good alone, but it really sang on a salad of baby greens with tomato, red onion, avocado, crumbled cotija and a sliced grilled chicken breast (I used Key West Chicken, recipe from this site). Awesome, easy-to-make combo that I will make again soon!
This dressing is amazing!!! I substituted brown sugar for honey and white vinegar for apple cider vinegar. It was delicious

I had to make lots of changes, but I like it now and have made it a few times. I use fresh limes and include lime zest (strong antioxidant) and I measured everything exactly the 2nd time and it was still way too acidic. The lime burned the back of my throat. So I added more sugar and oil. I also thought it was bland so I added white pepper and ginger. It tastes very good that way. Every dressing recipe has garlic so sometimes I use it and other times I don't.
YUM! I cut the olive oil to 1/4 cup and added 1/4 tsp. pepper. Makes a yummy broccoli slaw!

This recipes tastes delicious. I have tried it as is and recently I added pure passion fruit juice to it. HEAVEN!! Made it taste even better. I think the next patch, I will use pure passion fruit juice instead of the lime. That should be out of this world!

Wonderful! We started Keto so I omitted the brown sugar. Next time I'll add an entire bunch of cilantro as we just love the stuff! So easy and amazing. We also changed to lime juice to Key Lime... The Floridian in me just had to.
This is a wonderful dressing. The flavors really pop. The only thing I changed myself was I added a pinch of pepper and cut back on the oil by about half. I put this on a pasta salad. Fantastic.

I really liked the flavor profile, but think that you don't need all that oil. I double the recipe for all ingredients (and may have added even more cilantro -- I have a bumper crop) and used 1/2 cup (regular) olive oil. Turned out delicious. Looking forward to this on fish tacos and also on a grain bowl.
Very good. Perfect sweetness. I cut the olive oil on half and still good. Also didn’t like the garlic in it, so will omit that next time. Otherwise great! Thank you
It turned out pretty good. You can use lemon juice in a pinch. Also used less oil about 1/4 cup to make it lighter.
This is my all time favorite dressing. I originally got the recipe back in 2013. I love the consistency and the flavor is perfect. I actually use a whole bunch of cilantro.
This is my new goto salad dressing!
Delicious! I did add a teaspoon of cumin and used white wine vinegar, but other than that, I followed the recipe.
This is one of our favorites for veggie tacos too.

I made this just like the recipe. It was awesome! I used it as a marinade for a large steak that I grilled and then sliced over a mixed green salad. Then used the remainder as the dressing. It was outstanding!! My two boys were over the moon about it. I made it twice more within about two weeks. Very quick and easy.

Dressing was excellent. It taste like a salad dressing at one of our favorite restaurants. I used 2 whole bunches of cilantro, 4 cloves of garlic, a couple of TBS of honey, rice vinegar, part olive and canola oil and no mustard. I was trying to duplicate the dressing at the restaurant. It was really good. Nice and green!! Makes you feel like you are eating healthy! But this recipe is good as written.
